To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we present the homomorphic encryption evaluation of Prince, a lightweight block cipher, and that we show how to achieve this using only a 20 level deep circuit.

(1) we present a leveled implementation for homomorphic evaluation of Prince, a lightweight cipher, and (2) our implementation achieves a speedup of 2 orders of magnitude over BGV-style libraries and 1 order of magnitude over the NTRU-based AES implementation.

(i) the Prince cipher is suitable for practical homomorphic evaluation; (ii) the homomorphic evaluation time of Prince is significantly shorter than that of AES; and (iii) the homomorphic bandwidth savings that may accrue by scheme conversion are not realized in the case of Prince, as a result of the relatively large size of the Prince key.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the homomorphic evaluation and implementation of lightweight block ciphers, and the impact of scheme conversion on the resulting homomorphic implementation.

our leveled evaluation of Prince, using NTRU as the underlying scheme, is a significant improvement over previous work in terms of both bandwidth and time.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have shown how the Prince block cipher can be homomorphically evaluated with a reasonable evaluation time and with a bandwidth saving of 3 orders of magnitude over the homomorphic AES implementation.
the homomorphic evaluation time of block ciphers can be reduced from minutes (or even hours) to a few seconds, using lightweight block ciphers.
Prince is the first lightweight cipher to be homomorphically evaluated.
The main takeaway from our work is that
lightweight ciphers are a viable alternative to AES when considering homomorphic evaluation.
lightweight ciphers can enable near-practical homomorphic evaluation of symmetric-key primitives.
the homomorphic evaluation cost of a block cipher can be drastically reduced by using a lightweight cipher as a building block.
